subject: Function-calling playbook: SDK, auth, routing, embeddings & rerank — next steps

Subject: Follow-up: SDK samples + function-calling patterns (Finotek)

Hey Stephanie — thanks again for the discovery earlier today. A quick follow-up from our side with priorities so we can prep for a technical deep-dive: 

- High-level use cases: account lookups, ACH/payment initiation, AML/KYC checks, and a search/recommendation flow for statements.
- We want the model to call discrete tools for: send_payment, account_lookup, check_risk, and fetch_statements. Prefer deterministic structured output when actions are taken.
- Security: our procurement team will require details on auth options (client credentials vs per-tenant keys vs mTLS) and data residency.
- Performance targets: tail latency <= 250ms for fast lookups, 99th percentile; for payments we can accept up to 1s but need stronger guarantees.

Can you share an integration playbook that covers: SDK examples (node/python), recommended auth flow, routing/region fallback, structured output schemas, and an approach for embeddings + rerank for search? Also curious how you recommend orchestrating parallel vs sequential tool calls (e.g., check_risk + account_lookup).

Also, anyone on your team able to attend a 30-min technical follow-up this week (we can be flexible)?

Thanks — Sam

Head of Integrations, Finotek

Sam / Priya — great to meet you both. Recap + concrete next steps below. I attached a small bundle with SDK snippets and a one-page integration diagram; the Drive link is also in thread metadata.

Recap (from the discovery):
- Primary flows: 1) Search+Rerank for statements, 2) Transaction initiation (send_payment) with risk checks, 3) Account lookup + profile enrichment.
- Non-negotiables: per-tenant access controls, audit logs for every tool call, and the ability to pin a model version for payments flow.

Recommended integration patterns (high level):
1) SDK & Auth:
   - Use Redwood SDK (we provide Node/Python) for request signing + streaming. Default auth: per-tenant API keys issued via your SSO/KMS. For Private deployments we support mTLS and customer-managed KMS. For server-to-server flows, client-credentials (OAuth2) works well with short-lived tokens.
   - Auth recommendation matrix: payments => mTLS or short-lived tenant keys; lookups => client-credentials with scoped scopes; public UI features => proxy through your backend + token-bounded calls.

2) Tool/function definitions (schema-first):
   - Define tools via a JSON Schema-like contract. Examples: 
     - send_payment: {amount, currency, from_account_id, to_account_id, idempotency_key}
     - account_lookup: {account_id | external_id, include_balances:boolean}
     - check_risk: {subject_id, transaction_amount}
   - Enforce strict output schemas from the model (function-calling mode). Fallback: if schema validation fails, model returns a standardized error object with suggested human-in-loop flag.

3) Tool choice & orchestration:
   - Decision matrix: 
     - Deterministic side-effect actions (payments): model suggests action but server-side must validate signature/limits and execute via API.
     - Read-only lookups: can be called directly in parallel (low risk).
   - Parallel vs sequential: run low-risk / idempotent read tools in parallel (account_lookup, fetch_statements). Chain riskier calls behind a validation step (check_risk -> send_payment).

4) Error handling & idempotency:
   - Idempotency keys for all stateful calls. Retries with exponential backoff for transient errors (max 3 attempts).
   - Circuit breaker: after N consecutive failures (configurable) route to a safe fallback (text response + manual queue).
   - Observability: token-level trace ids, per-tool latency and success metrics, and model-output scoring for rerank decisions.

5) Embeddings & rerank approach:
   - Ingest: create per-tenant embedding index (we recommend 1536-d float32 or an 8-bit quantized profile for cost).
   - Search: ANN to get top-K (e.g., k=100), then rerank top-10 with the model using similarity + recency + business signals.
   - Refresh: incremental embedding updates on content change; batch reindex nightly for large backfills.

Attachments in the bundle: SDK snippets (node/python), JSON tool-contract examples, integration diagram.

Proposed next steps:
- Schedule 30-min tech deep-dive this Wed/Thu — I'll bring a sample Node snippet for the tool-wrapper and a small demo of function-calling + schema validation.
- Action items for us: produce a minimal PoC repo that implements account_lookup + check_risk + send_payment stubs; provide an embedding/rerank demo using your sample statements.

If that sounds good I'll send a calendar invite. Who from Finotek would join the deep-dive (engineering + security recommended)?

Quick notes — agree with the checklist. A few concrete defaults to include in the snippets: 

- Timeouts: default per-tool call timeout = 3000ms; overall model orchestration timeout = 7000ms.
- Retries: 2 retries with exponential backoff (base 300ms -> 600ms). Do not retry on 4xx semantic errors; only on 5xx / network errors.
- Idempotency: require idempotency_key for any stateful endpoint and validate on server side before execution.
- Circuit breaker: trip after 5 failures in 1 minute for that tool; cool-down 2 minutes.
- Observability: ensure every model request includes a trace_id and exec_id. Emit an event for each tool call with latency and result code.

Also: for function-calling fallback, prefer a strict JSON-schema validation step. If validation fails but the payload looks close, return a structured validation_error object with suggestions and send the candidate to a manual-review queue if the action is stateful. For read-only failures, we can degrade to text results (model-provided summary) to keep the UI responsive.

I'll push a tiny schema helper to the PoC repo and a sample circuit-breaker implementation.

— Rishi
